candidates.rationale: Price impact per dollar traded, scored against the stock's own recent history rather than cross-sectionally: when a name currently needs less volume to move its price, liquidity providers are charging a wider discount that is earned back as depth normalizes; the within-stock ranking strips the size exposure that a cross-sectional dollar-volume level would carry.

A day at the top of the recent dollar-volume distribution combined with a wide intraday range is expensive liquidity demand, and the impact the aggressor paid is transitory rather than informational, so it reverses over the next several days.

When heavy trading days are also the days the stock trades further above its open than below it, the order flow is informed accumulation rather than noise, and the resulting imbalance is worked over multiple sessions.

Operating-efficiency information diffuses slowly into names nobody is currently trading, so the efficiency tilt is worth holding among quiet stocks and is already impounded (and thus reversed) in ones seeing heavy turnover right now.

Accrual mispricing survives only where arbitrage is costly, so the earnings-quality short is concentrated in the least liquid names and switched off in the heavily traded ones where it is already competed away.

Heavy share volume alongside a multi-day decline is liquidation-driven, non-information supply from constrained holders, and the liquidity provider who absorbs it is paid the reversal; the same volume behind an advance is distribution.

The dollar-volume-to-volume ratio is the day's volume-weighted transaction price; when it settles below the opening print, sellers were paying the spread to exit, and that transitory pressure is reversed once the supply is cleared.

If the days a stock sits at the top of its own recent price range are also its heaviest-traded days, the advance is attention- and flow-driven rather than informational, and prices funded by liquidity demand decay back.

A volume surge while the stock sits at the bottom of its own 21-day range is forced or panic supply that gets absorbed and rebounds, while the identical surge at the top of the range is crowding into a name already bid up, which fades.

Book value measured against the price investors actually paid (the volume-weighted price implied by dollar volume over share volume), held where trading interest is low: the discount is still unarbitraged in neglected names and is already being repriced in crowded ones.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: EXPLORE. Propose 10 NEW factor expressions.

Direction for this island

turnover bucket). Aim at the emptiest ones: a factor that fills an empty niche
is worth more to this search than a slightly better version of a full one.

Sub-expressions already heavily used by the published Alpha101 set. Reusing one
of these wholesale will be rejected as a paraphrase; they are listed so you can
avoid them, not so you can vary them cosmetically.
  (($high + $low) / 2)   (in 5 published alphas)
  ($high + $low)   (in 5 published alphas)
  DELAY($close, 1)   (in 5 published alphas)
  TS_DELTA($close, 1)   (in 5 published alphas)
  TS_MEAN($volume, 20)   (in 5 published alphas)

  (1e-08 + TS_MEAN($volume, 20))   (in 4 published alphas)

  TS_DELTA($close, 7)   (in 4 published alphas)
  (((DELAY($close, 20) - DELAY($close, 10)) / 10) - ((DELAY($close, 10) - $close) / 10))   (in 3 published alphas)
  ((DELAY($close, 20) - DELAY($close, 10)) / 10)   (in 3 published alphas)
  (($close - DELAY($close, 1)) * -(1))   (in 3 published alphas)

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Keep lookbacks at 21 bars or fewer. Accepted expressions used only 2 and 21 bar windows; 42, 63, 126, and 189 bar lookbacks appeared exclusively in rejected proposals.
  2. Drop conditional regime splits. The single IF_ELSE proposal, switching between short-horizon reversal and momentum on high-low versus its 21d mean, had the worst cheap screen of the round at 0.48.
  3. RANK($roa) is too small to serve as a crossover parent. Both children built around it kept almost none of it while adding long-window volatility and price-extreme terms. Graft it whole as one operand of a larger donor expression, or cross from a bigger parent subtree instead.
  4. Normalize intraday-range terms by a raw OHLC field, as the accepted ones do with $open and ($high - $low). Do not divide OHLC quantities by $close: $close is adjusted while OHLC is raw, so mixing the scales is a units error that imports future dividend information.
  5. Multiplying a cross-sectional fundamental rank by a price-normalized range term is what paid: all three accepts above 4.0 had that shape. Every additive fundamental +/- volume-rank combo died on the cheap screen (|t| 0.52 and 0.06).
  6. Volume on its own is weak or duplicative: TS_ARGMAX($volume,21) scored 0.70, the 21d volume CV 1.43, and TS_RANK($volume,21) hit rho 0.94 against the dollar-volume z-score. Volume paid only when correlated against a second series (TS_CORR($volume, $high-$low, 21) = 4.98).
  7. $return as an input is dead on this fit window: TS_MEAN($return,21) gave |t| 0.35 and TS_CORR($return,$volume,10) gave |t| 0.09. Build the same ideas from price levels and $high-$low instead.
  8. Ratios of two windows of the same series failed the cheap screen every time (volume 5/21 -> 0.66, range 21/5 -> 0.19). Normalize against a different series or a price level, not against a longer window of itself.
  9. Near-copies of archive members caused 11 of 20 rejects: swapping one price leaf ($high for $close), one window constant (10->21, 21->189), inverting a ratio, or wrapping an existing term in TS_MEAN at the same window (rho 0.824). Change an operator or a whole input, not a parameter.
  10. A difference of two fundamental ranks submitted alone tracks its dominant leg (RANK($roa)-RANK($accrual_gap) hit rho 0.802 against RANK($roa)). The same spread cleared at 4.11 once multiplied by a price term, so gate fundamental spreads rather than proposing them bare.
  11. Do not put adjusted $close and raw OHLC in the same ratio or difference; it is a scale error that leaks future dividend information, whatever fitness it reports.
  12. Slot economics: fast/price_volume is held at only 1.43 and slow/price_volume at 0.70, so those are the cheap wins. slow/mixed is now held at 4.76 and 4.11 by fundamental-times-range factors, so further variants of that shape will mostly trip the correlation and subtree gates.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
